metadata.label: SSI reflectance
metadata.coverage: Two complementary Galileo clear-filter close-ups cover both ends of Gaspra. Their calibrated brightness retains the original illumination. The grid marks gaps and rejected pixels.

celestial.sunSource: Pinned JPL Horizons heliocentric elements and the source mission body-fixed rotation model

controls.label: Monochrome
controls.notes: Galileo’s highest-resolution pair, 107318313 and 107318326, mapped onto the Thomas shape. The source is high-pass filtered and retains photographed illumination; it is not calibrated albedo or natural color. Best original detail is approximately 55 m/pixel and varies greatly. The gray grid marks poor or missing coverage. Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting.

controls.label: SSI reflectance
controls.notes: These Galileo close-ups cover opposite ends of Gaspra. They were taken through a clear filter and show the sunlight and shadows from the flyby. The grid marks areas without usable photographs.

controls.label: Elevation
controls.notes: Color shows the published shape radius minus a 6.1 km reference sphere, including Gaspra’s broad irregular shape. This is shape-derived height, not gravitational elevation or a photographic observation. Shape constraints vary with the flyby coverage; unseen regions are less certain. Brightness adds cartographic relief; Shadows adds approximate fixed-epoch Sun lighting.

sources.purpose: Published Hapke photometric model of Gaspra, used to normalize the Galileo photograph mosaic.

references.evidence: Helfenstein et al. (1994) give the single-scattering albedo 0.36, opposition amplitude 1.63 and roughness 29 degrees, fitted to Earth-based photometry at 2-25 degrees phase and Galileo data at 33-51 degrees phase.
Hasselmann et al. (2016) tabulate the Helfenstein et al. (1994) Gaspra solution, including the opposition width 0.06, asymmetry factor -0.18 and 560 nm wavelength that the abstract does not state.

sources.credit: Published Hapke parameters: Helfenstein et al. (1994), doi:10.1006/icar.1994.1005. Selection and transcription: cssEarth.
sources.acquisition: Parameter values transcribed from the cited publication into a project document; no data file was downloaded.
sources.title: Published Hapke photometric model of Gaspra, used to normalize the Galileo photograph mosaic.
